headline: 412.3mm rain: Chattogram records highest daily rainfall in 42 years
summary: Severe waterlogging has submerged major roads, suspended HSC exams and university classes, and left thousands stranded in the city and adjoining upazilas.
details: The Chattogram Meteorological Office recorded 412.3mm of rainfall in 24 hours, marking the third-highest daily rainfall in the observatory's history. This was followed by another 237.5mm of rain, prolonging the crisis across the city and surrounding areas.

Knee- to waist-deep water submerged major city roads and low-lying neighborhoods, including Agrabad, Halishahar, and Chawkbazar. The flooding disrupted public transport and forced many businesses to close as rainwater entered ground-floor shops.

In Anwara and Karnaphuli upazilas, continuous rain and hill runoff flooded 16 unions, leaving thousands stranded. Power infrastructure was also damaged in Anwara, causing prolonged electricity outages for residents.
The severe weather led to the postponement of HSC examinations under the Chattogram Education Board and the suspension of all classes and exams at the University of Chittagong.

Authorities have stepped up monitoring in landslide-prone areas, using loudspeakers to urge residents on risky slopes to move to shelter centers. Dried food and essential supplies have been dispatched to these shelters.
The crisis comes as wall collapses and landslides claimed six lives across Chattogram city, Rangunia, Baghaichhari, and Cox's Bazar over the past 24 hours.
The Meteorological Office has advised maritime ports to keep local cautionary signal No. 3 hoisted, warning that the current spell of rain is likely to continue until Friday.

headline: 600 tourists stranded in Sajek Valley as rain cuts off road links
summary: Heavy rainfall has submerged sections of the Sajek-Baghaihat road, leaving hundreds of visitors unable to leave the popular tourist destination.
details: Around 600 tourists are currently stranded at Sajek Valley in Rangamati's Baghaichhari upazila. Heavy rainfall has submerged sections of the Sajek-Baghaihat road and a bridge in the Machalong area, cutting off access.

The tourists, who arrived on Monday and Tuesday, are currently staying at various resorts and cottages in the valley. They will remain there until the rainfall subsides and the water recedes from the road.

In a gesture of support, resort and cottage owners have decided not to charge room rent for the stranded tourists during their extended stay. Visitors will only be required to pay for food and other necessary services.
The Rangamati district administration has temporarily closed the Sajek Valley tourist destination until further notice due to the heavy rain and fears of landslides.
